transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, my mind keeps going blank. It happens at work. I'll just be looking at the road-closure forms, or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and I suddenly can't remember what to do. Things I've done for years. It's just... gone.
During these episodes, do you ever lose awareness of what's going on around you or black out, or are you fully awake and alert the whole time, just unable to remember what to do?
I'm... I'm awake. I don't black out or anything. I just... I just can't think of what to do next. It's like my brain just stops.
During these moments when your mind goes blank, do you notice your heart racing, sweating, or trembling, or any other physical sensations?
No... not really. Just the blankness.
During these episodes, do others ever notice you staring blankly, making repetitive movements, or twitching, even if you yourself don't remember it happening?
No... nobody has ever said anything like that to me. I don't think so.
Did these episodes start around the same time as any particular stressful event or big change in your life, like at work or at home?
I suppose... yeah. It's been going on for about a year and eight months now. It started... right after my closest friend died.
Since your friend's death, have you experienced intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares related to that loss?
No... I don't really have anything like that. Just... regular dreams, I guess. Nothing specific.
Since your friend passed away, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or less interested in things you used to enjoy?

I guess so... yeah. Most mornings I just... I wake up and there's this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It's just sadness, I suppose. It feels like... like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor.

Besides the sadness, have you noticed changes in your sleep or appetite—like trouble falling asleep, sleeping much more or less than usual, or a big change in how much you're eating—since your friend passed away?

I don't know... food just stopped meaning much to me, I guess. I skip meals without really noticing. I only realized because my flagger pants are loose... and my family keeps asking why I look so drawn.
Have you had any thoughts of death, or of not wanting to be alive, since your friend passed away?

I... yeah, I guess. I just... I don't really have the energy to fight those thoughts anymore. Sometimes I just think it might be better if I didn't wake up. I've started saying it out loud without meaning to... and I know it scares my family. But it's just... how I feel.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a cluster of depressive symptoms—persistent low mood, anhedonia, significant appetite/weight loss, cognitive symptoms (difficulty concentrating/'mind going blank'), and passive suicidal ideation with verbalized wish to not wake up—that began after a major psychosocial stressor (death of close friend) and have persisted for ~20 months. There is no evidence of dissociative episodes (patient remains alert, no loss of awareness, no observed staring/automatisms), no autonomic arousal suggesting panic, and no intrusive memories/flashbacks/nightmares to support PTSD. The severity (active suicidal ideation, marked functional and appetite disturbance) and duration exceed adjustment disorder criteria, supporting a diagnosis of a single major depressive episode, severe, without psychotic features.
